scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.dialogue: In the days after the July 1 protests began, students intensified their campaign. From July 7 to 10, 2024, thousands of students carried out the “Bangla Blockade” — boycotting classes and blocking major highways, railways, and key intersections across the country, including Shahbagh in Dhaka, bringing city traffic close to a standstill.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.dialogue: On July 10, 2024, the Supreme Court temporarily suspended the quota ruling for one month, following legal petitions — a partial concession. On the same day, the Rapid Action Battalion, a paramilitary force previously accused of serious human rights violations, was deployed alongside police to help contain the protests. The state was offering a concession and hardening its response at the same time.

choice.prompt: Whose account would you like to follow first?

evidence.title: Bangla Blockade at Shahbagh, 7 July 2024
evidence.sourceCaption: The Daily Star / Prabir Das. Original archive filename: "bangla_blockade_2.jpg". From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: A group of dozens of male university students gathered on an asphalt road during a blockade at the Shahbagh intersection on 7 July 2024. Large white text painted directly on the road surface reads: "দফা এক দাবি এক, কোটা বৈষম্য নিপাত যাক" ("One Point One Demand, Down with Quota Discrimination"). On the left, a student sitting on the ground holds a handwritten cardboard placard with Bangla text ("কোটার কবর" — "Grave of Quota"). Several students are wearing red and green headband bands representing the Bangladesh flag, clapping, and chanting slogans. In the background, a rickshaw and street buildings are partially visible.

evidence.title: The New Nation — "Students denounce quota reinstatement"
evidence.sourceCaption: Titled in the source archive as `"3rdJuly.jpg"`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: Front-page newspaper clipping featuring a headline, article text, and a photograph of a massive crowd of students gathered on a roadway, with some individuals holding a banner. Published 3 July 2024.
evidence.text: The New Nation's 3 July 2024 edition reports on early demonstrations by university students who blocked the Shahbagh intersection in response to the High Court's decision to reinstate the quota system. The publication captures the initial mobilization of students from multiple institutions in the days following the High Court's June 2024 reinstatement of the 30 percent quota.

evidence.title: Prothom Alo — "35 Public Universities Paralyzed"
evidence.sourceCaption: Titled in the source archive as `"students fighting for their rights".jpg`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: Newspaper clipping with Bengali text featuring a prominent headline ("৩৫ পাবলিক বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় অচল" — "35 Public Universities Paralyzed") and a photograph of a large, organized group of individuals participating in a sit-in or gathering. Published 2 July 2024.
evidence.text: Prothom Alo's 2 July 2024 edition reports on a widespread strike by teachers and employees across 35 public universities, who were protesting the newly issued universal pension scheme. This concurrent movement added to the institutional disruptions occurring throughout the country during the same period as the early student quota-protest demonstrations. The same-day news roundup is recorded here as a parallel labor dispute rather than an event in the student-protest thread.

evidence.title: Samoyer Alo — "Protest on Campus at Night"
evidence.sourceCaption: Titled in the source archive as `"students from all places gathering ".jpg`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: Newspaper front page displaying a large, dense crowd of people gathered outdoors at night, accompanied by a headline and detailed article text in Bengali. The headline reads "রাতে ক্যাম্পাসে বিক্ষোভ" ("Protest on Campus at Night"). Published 15 July 2024.
evidence.text: Samoyer Alo's 15 July 2024 edition reports on late-night protests that erupted across various university campuses. The coverage captures the expansion of the quota reform demonstrations from daytime blockades into continuous nighttime assemblies, the same day as the BCL attacks on multiple campuses covered in chapter-03.

evidence.title: A crowd of young men gathered on a street in Mymensingh
evidence.sourceCaption: Outlet / photographer / archive credit: unknown. Original archive filename: `"students in Mymensigh protesting".jpg`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: A dense crowd of young men gathered on a street facing a building. Several individuals hold up mobile phones to record, one individual holds a placard or document. A prominent orange signpost and a multi-story building with text painted on the facade are visible in the background. Date: July 2024 (exact date unknown). Location: Mymensingh (exact location unconfirmed).

evidence.title: Our Time — "Protesters issue 24hr ultimatum to reform quota system"
evidence.sourceCaption: Titled in the source archive as `"ultimatum".jpg`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: English-language newspaper clipping with a red headline, article text detailing the ultimatum, and a photograph of female demonstrators holding a banner alongside a hand-drawn satirical poster. Published 15 July 2024.
evidence.text: Our Time's 15 July 2024 edition reports on a 24-hour ultimatum issued to the government by the Anti-Discriminatory Student Movement, demanding reforms to the quota system. The article highlights the formal demands submitted by student coordinators during the mid-July escalation of the protests. The ultimatum is recorded here as one event within the 15 July escalation that also saw BCL attacks on university campuses covered in chapter-03.

evidence.title: Concession and Escalation
evidence.sourceCaption: European Union Agency for Asylum (EUAA), Bangladesh Country Focus Country of Origin Information Report, August 2025, “7–10 July 2024” and “11–13 July 2024” sections.
evidence.text: On July 10, 2024, the Supreme Court temporarily suspended the quota ruling for one month following legal petitions, and the Rapid Action Battalion — a paramilitary force previously accused of serious human rights violations — was deployed alongside police that same day. By July 11, police announced they would act against road blockades, arguing the suspension removed justification to continue, though tens of thousands of protesters defied this and kept blocking roads.

evidence.title: The New Nation — "Full text of HC verdict on quota published"
evidence.sourceCaption: Titled in the source archive as `"everyone is deceiving ".jpg`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: Newspaper front-page clipping featuring a headline describing publication of the High Court's full verdict on the quota reform matter. The clipping is dated 15 July 2024.
evidence.text: The New Nation's published front-page headline on 15 July 2024 reports the publication of the High Court's full verdict on the quota system. The High Court's earlier ruling in June 2024 had reinstated the 30 percent government-jobs quota for descendants of freedom fighters, reversing the 2018 circular. The 15 July 2024 publication of the full text of that verdict is recorded here as a separate event from the Supreme Court's subsequent 10 July temporary suspension and 21 July final ruling.

evidence.title: Kaler Kantho — "Students Protest Demanding Quota Abolition"
evidence.sourceCaption: Titled in the source archive as `propaganda.jpg`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: Newspaper page featuring a headline, article text, and summary boxes describing student demonstrations, road blockades, and planned protest activities. The headline is in Bengali: "কোটা বাতিল চেয়ে শিক্ষার্থীদের বিক্ষোভ" ("Students Protest Demanding Quota Abolition"). The page is dated 2 July 2024.
evidence.text: Kaler Kantho's 2 July 2024 edition reports the student demonstrations demanding reform of the government job quota system during the opening days of July 2024. The article describes road blockades and planned protest activities in the early period of the movement.

evidence.title: Samakal — "Students' Extremism Is Increasing: Home Minister"
evidence.sourceCaption: Titled in the source archive as `"when everything slips, you can only blame the outsider".jpg`. From duniyakapanojuly.org (July-36 archive). Permission documented in docs/permissions/july-36-archive.md.
evidence.archiveNote: Newspaper clipping featuring the Home Minister's quoted remarks, publication information, and accompanying article text discussing the ongoing demonstrations. The headline is in Bengali: "শিক্ষার্থীদের উগ্রপন্থিতা বেড়ে যাচ্ছে : স্বরাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী" ("Students' Extremism Is Increasing: Home Minister"). The page is dated 15 July 2024.
evidence.text: Samakal's 15 July 2024 edition reports official government remarks concerning the expanding student demonstrations as the quota movement continued during mid-July 2024. The Home Minister's quoted remarks are reproduced alongside the article text.
